correctness.rationale: For e_S and a restriction g|_T, both compositions coincide where defined and have equal domains exactly when 1_S(x)=1_S(gx) for each x in T. At an equal-bit transition the factor for choosing the domain is 1+v, otherwise it is 1; multiplying by u for the target bit 1 yields the specified K. Taking the trace closes each cycle and counts even fixed points with a single bit and a single domain choice. Freeness gives mN/d cycles for an order-d element and unique extensions of nonempty restrictions; the empty restriction contributes (1+u)^(mN) once, so only N−1 copies are subtracted. At u=v=1 the eigenvalues are 3 and 1. The logarithm log 3 + log(1+3^(−t))/t decreases strictly in t>0, making the moment bases b_d positive and distinct and the shifted Vandermonde matrix invertible. The leading nonidentity term has d=p by Cauchy's theorem and strict decrease. In the normalization N4^(mN)−(N−1)2^(mN), the correction is negligible on the scale b_p^m since 2^N<b_p<4^N. For N=1 this reduces to an all-commuting Boolean semilattice. As exact substitutions, C_1(C4)=256+100+164−48=472 and C_1(C2×C2)=256+300−48=508. The supplied script was inspected, not run; the displayed finite expected checks do not prove the general theorem.

value.rationale: A natural rank-sensitive statistic on a restriction inverse monoid is shown to encode exactly the group order distribution. Recovering it from a finite sequence of scalar counts is more informative than noting that the unit group equals G or enumerating a single monoid. The least-prime term further identifies which element orders govern departure from the limiting probability. The result is useful without claiming to distinguish isomorphism classes.
